text:
olivia.r: Heads-up from the onboarding run: our demo UI treats any 4xx as "Authorization error" and shows a generic banner. Support saw 3 identical tickets where users had expired tokens but were told to 'contact support'. We should make SDK errors actionable and language-consistent.

mike.s: Yep saw those. Users don't know whether to retry, re-login, or request additional permissions.

rita.t: Short proposal: standardize an error payload returned by the API and map it to idiomatic SDK surfaces. Fields we should include at the transport level: error_code (dot.path), brief_message (user safe), intent ("reauth"|"refresh"|"request_scope"|"backoff"|"fatal"), and optional retry_after seconds.

kevin: I like the intent enum. Concrete suggestion for mappings:
```
# server-side canonical mapping (example)
401 + body.code == "token.expired" -> error_code: "auth.token_expired", intent: "refresh", brief_message: "Session expired, reconnect to continue."
401 + body.code == "credential.invalid" -> error_code: "auth.invalid_credentials", intent: "fatal", brief_message: "Sign-in failed, check credentials."
403 -> error_code: "auth.missing_scope", intent: "request_scope", brief_message: "App needs additional permission: inference.write"
429 -> error_code: "rate.limit_exceeded", intent: "backoff", brief_message: "Rate limit reached, try again later.", retry_after: 30
5xx -> error_code: "service.unavailable", intent: "retry_later", brief_message: "Service temporarily unavailable."
```

rita.t: SDK-side: expose both (1) a typed error class/variant and (2) machine fields. Examples: Python raise AuthTokenExpired(err_code="auth.token_expired", intent="refresh", user_message="...") ; JS throw new AuthInvalidError({code, intent, message}); Go return typed error implementing ErrorCode() and Intent() methods.

mike.s: Important UX rule: brief_message must be copy-tested and safe for end-users (no internal IDs, no raw stack). Also include an optional developer_explain field (not shown to users) with a short diagnostic for logs.

rita.t: For parity, let's keep canonical error_code namespace: auth.* | rate.* | service.*. Add a small test harness in sdks/samples/onboarding/tests that mocks responses and asserts error_code + intent + class across JS/Py/Go.

kevin: I pushed a tiny sampleapp patch in the onboarding demo that maps intent->CTA: refresh -> show "Reconnect" button; request_scope -> show "Grant permission" flow; backoff -> show countdown. Cuts a bunch of friction. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/1240 (draft).

mike.s: One more operational note: Ops can annotate 5xx responses with a header X-Transient: true so SDKs can prefer retryable=true; default for 5xx should be retryable=false unless annotated.

olivia.r: TL;DR action items:
- API: return stable error_code + brief_message + intent + optional retry_after + developer_explain
- SDKs: expose typed errors + machine fields; Go pattern as return values with helper funcs IsRetryable()/Intent()
- Update onboarding sampleapp to surface CTAs based on intent
- Add automated parity tests across JS/Py/Go that assert mapping

ops-bot: summary (auto): Proposed stable codes: auth.token_expired, auth.invalid_credentials, auth.missing_scope, rate.limit_exceeded, service.unavailable. Fields: error_code, brief_message, intent, retry_after, developer_explain. Create SDK parity ticket and update sampleapp tests.

rita.t: I'll write a tiny RFC + mapping table tonight and include code snippets for each SDK. Will tag y'all for review. :sparkles:

kevin: Thanks — will coordinate with support to retitle the onboarding alert once this lands. :thumbsup:
